subproblems.title: One-sided limits at 0⁺ from subsequences of positive null sequences
subproblems.statement: Let f : ℝ → [0, ∞] and L ∈ [0, ∞]. Suppose that for every sequence (λ_j)_{j∈ℕ} of positive reals with λ_j → 0 there is a strictly increasing φ : ℕ → ℕ with f(λ_{φ(j)}) → L as j → ∞. Then f(t) → L as t → 0⁺ (Tendsto f (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 L)).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (f : ℝ → ℝ≥0∞) (L : ℝ≥0∞), (∀ lams : ℕ → ℝ, (∀ j, 0 < lams j) → Tendsto lams atTop (𝓝 0) → ∃ φ : ℕ → ℕ, StrictMono φ ∧ Tendsto (fun j => f (lams (φ j))) atTop (𝓝 L)) → Tendsto f (𝓝[>] 0) (𝓝 L)
subproblems.natural_proof:
1. The filter 𝓝[>]0 on ℝ is countably generated: 𝓝 0 is countably generated (ℝ is first countable) and 𝓝[>]0 = 𝓝 0 ⊓ 𝓟(Ioi 0). Hence, by the subsequence criterion for countably generated filters (Mathlib `Filter.tendsto_of_subseq_tendsto`), it suffices to show: for every sequence ns : ℕ → ℝ with Tendsto ns atTop (𝓝[>]0) there is ms : ℕ → ℕ with f(ns(ms(j))) → L.
2. Let ns → 𝓝[>]0. Since Ioi 0 ∈ 𝓝[>]0, ns(n) > 0 for all large n; fix N ∈ ℕ with ns(n) > 0 for all n ≥ N. Since 𝓝[>]0 ≤ 𝓝 0, also ns(n) → 0.
3. Define λ_j := ns(j + N). Then λ_j > 0 for every j (because j + N ≥ N), and λ_j → 0, as the composition of ns → 0 with the map j ↦ j + N, which tends to atTop.
4. By the hypothesis applied to (λ_j) there is a strictly increasing φ with f(λ_{φ(j)}) → L. Put ms(j) := φ(j) + N. Then ns(ms(j)) = ns(φ(j) + N) = λ_{φ(j)}, so f(ns(ms(j))) = f(λ_{φ(j)}) → L.
5. By step 1, f(t) → L as t → 0⁺. ∎
proof_key_steps: 𝓝[>]0 is countably generated, so Filter.tendsto_of_subseq_tendsto reduces the claim to sequences ns → 𝓝[>]0.
Such ns is eventually positive and tends to 0; the shifted sequence λ_j = ns(j + N) is a positive null sequence.
The hypothesis applied to λ gives φ, and ms(j) = φ(j) + N is the required subsequence.

subproblems.title: Rescaled boxes Z(s, s') are squeezed between two squares
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, Q a linear subspace of ℝ^P with orthogonal projection π := Q.starProjection, and a, e ∈ ℝ^P with a ∈ Q, |a| = |e| = 1 and ⟨a, e⟩ = 0. Let s, η, s' ∈ ℝ with 0 < η, 0 < s', 20s' < 1, 30s' < η and 6s' < s. Put η_{s'} := dilation a s' (η_{s'}(x) = s'^{-1}(x − a)), Z(s, s') := {x : ⟨x, a⟩ > 0, ||x| − 1| < s', |arctan(⟨x, e⟩/⟨x, a⟩)| < s', |x − πx| < s|x|}, U := {w : |w| < 3, |⟨w, a⟩| < 1 − η, |⟨w, e⟩| < 1 − η} and K := {w : |w| ≤ 3, |⟨w, a⟩| ≤ 1 + η, |⟨w, e⟩| ≤ 1 + η}. Then η_{s'}^{-1}(U) ⊆ Z(s, s') and Z(s, s') ∩ B_{3s'}(a) ⊆ η_{s'}^{-1}(K).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (a e : Euclid P) (s η s' : ℝ), a ∈ Q → ‖a‖ = 1 → ‖e‖ = 1 → inner ℝ a e = 0 → 0 < η → 0 < s' → 20 * s' < 1 → 30 * s' < η → 6 * s' < s → dilation a s' ⁻¹' {w : Euclid P | ‖w‖ < 3 ∧ |inner ℝ w a| < 1 - η ∧ |inner ℝ w e| < 1 - η} ⊆ {x : Euclid P | 0 < inner ℝ x a ∧ |‖x‖ - 1| < s' ∧ |Real.arctan (inner ℝ x e / inner ℝ x a)| < s' ∧ ‖x - Q.starProjection x‖ < s * ‖x‖} ∧ {x : Euclid P | 0 < inner ℝ x a ∧ |‖x‖ - 1| < s' ∧ |Real.arctan (inner ℝ x e / inner ℝ x a)| < s' ∧ ‖x - Q.starProjection x‖ < s * ‖x‖} ∩ ball a (3 * s') ⊆ dilation a s' ⁻¹' {w : Euclid P | ‖w‖ ≤ 3 ∧ |inner ℝ w a| ≤ 1 + η ∧ |inner ℝ w e| ≤ 1 + η}
subproblems.natural_proof:
Notation: f(x) := arctan(⟨x, e⟩/⟨x, a⟩) (real division). By definition dilation a s' x = −(s'^{-1}•a) + s'^{-1}•x, so η_{s'}(x) = s'^{-1}(x − a) and x = a + s'·η_{s'}(x). Note 0 < s' < 1/20 and s > 6s' > 0.
1. (Estimates.) Let w ∈ ℝ^P with |w| < 3 and put x := a + s'w, p := s'⟨w, a⟩, q := s'⟨w, e⟩.
(a) By Cauchy–Schwarz and |a| = |e| = 1: |p| ≤ s'|w| < 3s' and |q| < 3s'.
(b) ⟨x, a⟩ = |a|² + p = 1 + p > 1 − 3s' > 17/20 > 0, and ⟨x, e⟩ = ⟨a, e⟩ + q = q.
(c) |x| ≥ ⟨x, a⟩ > 17/20 (Cauchy–Schwarz with |a| = 1).
(d) |x|² = |a|² + 2s'⟨a, w⟩ + s'²|w|² = 1 + y with y := 2p + s'²|w|², and |y| < 6s' + 9s'² < 7s' (as 9s'² < s'). Let t := |x| ≥ 0, so t² = 1 + y. From (t − 1)(t + 1) = y and t + 1 ≥ 1 we get |t − 1| ≤ |y|; and t − 1 − y/2 = t − 1 − (t² − 1)/2 = −(t − 1)²/2, so |t − 1 − y/2| ≤ y²/2 < 49s'²/2. Also 0 ≤ y/2 − p = s'²|w|²/2 < 9s'²/2. Hence ||x| − 1 − p| < 29s'² ≤ 30s'².
(e) By (b), ⟨x, e⟩/⟨x, a⟩ = z := q/(1 + p), so f(x) = arctan z. Since 1 + p > 17/20: |z − q| = |q||p|/(1 + p) < 9s'²·20/17 < 11s'², and |z| < 3s'·20/17 < 4s'. By the mean value theorem (arctan' = 1/(1 + ξ²)) there is ξ between 0 and z with arctan z − z = (1/(1 + ξ²) − 1)z = −ξ²z/(1 + ξ²), so |arctan z − z| ≤ ξ²|z| ≤ |z|³ < 64s'³ < 4s'² (as s' < 1/20). Hence |f(x) − q| < 15s'² ≤ 30s'².
(f) Since a ∈ Q, πa = a; π is linear, so x − πx = s'(w − πw). By Pythagoras (|w|² = |πw|² + |w − πw|²), |w − πw| ≤ |w| < 3, hence |x − πx| < 3s'.
2. (η_{s'}^{-1}(U) ⊆ Z(s, s').) Let x ∈ η_{s'}^{-1}(U) and w := η_{s'}(x); then |w| < 3, |⟨w, a⟩| < 1 − η, |⟨w, e⟩| < 1 − η and x = a + s'w. With p, q as in step 1, |p| < s'(1 − η) and |q| < s'(1 − η). By 1(b), ⟨x, a⟩ > 0. By 1(d), ||x| − 1| ≤ |p| + 30s'² < s'(1 − η) + 30s'² = s' − s'(η − 30s') < s', using 30s' < η. By 1(e), |f(x)| ≤ |q| + 30s'² < s' in the same way. By 1(f), 1(c) and 6s' < s: |x − πx| < 3s' < s/2 < (17/20)s < s|x|. Thus x ∈ Z(s, s').
3. (Z(s, s') ∩ B_{3s'}(a) ⊆ η_{s'}^{-1}(K).) Let x ∈ Z(s, s') with |x − a| < 3s' and put w := η_{s'}(x). Then x = a + s'w and |w| = |x − a|/s' < 3; in particular |w| ≤ 3 and step 1 applies. By 1(d) and ||x| − 1| < s': s'|⟨w, a⟩| = |p| ≤ ||x| − 1| + ||x| − 1 − p| < s' + 30s'², hence |⟨w, a⟩| < 1 + 30s' < 1 + η. By 1(e) and |f(x)| < s': s'|⟨w, e⟩| = |q| ≤ |f(x)| + |f(x) − q| < s' + 30s'², hence |⟨w, e⟩| < 1 + η. Thus η_{s'}(x) ∈ K, i.e. x ∈ η_{s'}^{-1}(K). ∎
proof_key_steps: Write x = a + s'w with w = η_{s'}(x) = s'^{-1}(x − a).
For |w| < 3 and s' < 1/20: ⟨x, a⟩ > 17/20, |x| > 17/20, ||x| − 1 − s'⟨w, a⟩| ≤ 30s'² (square-root expansion), |f(x) − s'⟨w, e⟩| ≤ 30s'² (|arctan z − z| ≤ |z|³) and |x − πx| < 3s'.
If w ∈ U, every defining inequality of Z(s, s') holds because 30s' < η and 6s' < s.

subproblems.title: H² of squares in a 2-plane and local finiteness of H²⌞Q
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, Q a linear subspace of ℝ^P with dim Q = 2, and a, e ∈ Q with |a| = |e| = 1 and ⟨a, e⟩ = 0. Let ν₀ := H²⌞Q (μHE[2].restrict Q). Then ν₀ is finite on compact sets, and for every r with 0 ≤ r ≤ 2: ν₀({w : |w| < 3, |⟨w, a⟩| < r, |⟨w, e⟩| < r}) = 4r² and ν₀({w : |w| ≤ 3, |⟨w, a⟩| ≤ r, |⟨w, e⟩| ≤ r}) = 4r² (both as ENNReal.ofReal (4r²)).
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (Q : Submodule ℝ (Euclid P)) (a e : Euclid P), Module.finrank ℝ Q = 2 → a ∈ Q → e ∈ Q → ‖a‖ = 1 → ‖e‖ = 1 → inner ℝ a e = 0 → IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts (μHE[2].restrict (Q : Set (Euclid P))) ∧ ∀ r : ℝ, 0 ≤ r → r ≤ 2 → μHE[2].restrict (Q : Set (Euclid P)) {w : Euclid P | ‖w‖ < 3 ∧ |inner ℝ w a| < r ∧ |inner ℝ w e| < r} = ENNReal.ofReal (4 * r ^ 2) ∧ μHE[2].restrict (Q : Set (Euclid P)) {w : Euclid P | ‖w‖ ≤ 3 ∧ |inner ℝ w a| ≤ r ∧ |inner ℝ w e| ≤ r} = ENNReal.ofReal (4 * r ^ 2)
subproblems.natural_proof:
1. (Basis.) a and e are orthonormal, hence linearly independent; span{a, e} ⊆ Q has dimension 2 = dim Q, so span{a, e} = Q.
2. (Parametrization.) Define ι : EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) → ℝ^P, ι(v) := v₀a + v₁e. ι is linear and |ι v|² = v₀²|a|² + 2v₀v₁⟨a, e⟩ + v₁²|e|² = v₀² + v₁² = |v|², so ι is norm preserving, hence an isometry (|ι v − ι v'| = |ι(v − v')| = |v − v'|). Its range is span{a, e} = Q (step 1), and ⟨ι v, a⟩ = v₀, ⟨ι v, e⟩ = v₁.
3. (Transfer to Lebesgue measure.) For every S ⊆ ℝ^P, S ∩ Q = ι(ι^{-1}(S)) because range ι = Q. By isometry invariance of the Euclidean Hausdorff measure (Isometry.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_image) and μHE[2] = volume on EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) (EuclideanSpace.euclideanHausdorffMeasure_eq_volume 2): μHE[2](S ∩ Q) = μHE[2](ι^{-1}(S)) = vol₂(ι^{-1}(S)). If S is measurable, ν₀(S) = μHE[2](S ∩ Q) (Measure.restrict_apply), so ν₀(S) = vol₂(ι^{-1}(S)).
4. (Finite on compacts.) Let K ⊆ ℝ^P be compact. K is closed, hence measurable, and K ⊆ B̄(0, ρ) for some ρ ≥ 0. Since ι preserves norms, ι^{-1}(K) ⊆ B̄(0, ρ) ⊆ EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2), so ν₀(K) = vol₂(ι^{-1}(K)) ≤ vol₂(B̄(0, ρ)) < ∞. Hence ν₀ is finite on compact sets. (Equivalently, and shortest in Lean: Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.regular_euclideanHausdorffMeasure_restrict_submodule applied to finrank Q = 2 shows that ν₀ is a regular measure, and every regular measure is finite on compact sets.)
5. (Open square.) Let 0 ≤ r ≤ 2 and S := {w : |w| < 3, |⟨w, a⟩| < r, |⟨w, e⟩| < r}, an open (so measurable) set. By step 2, ι^{-1}(S) = {v : |v| < 3, |v₀| < r, |v₁| < r} = {v : |v₀| < r, |v₁| < r}, since |v₀|, |v₁| < r implies |v|² = v₀² + v₁² < 2r² ≤ 8 < 9. The measurable equivalence EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) → (Fin 2 → ℝ), v ↦ (v₀, v₁), is volume preserving (PiLp.volume_preserving_ofLp), and it maps this set onto the box (−r, r) × (−r, r) = Set.pi univ (fun _ => Ioo (−r) r), whose volume is ofReal(2r)·ofReal(2r) = ofReal(4r²) (Real.volume_pi_Ioo). Hence ν₀(S) = ofReal(4r²). (For r = 0 both sides are 0.)
6. (Closed square.) Let K_r := {w : |w| ≤ 3, |⟨w, a⟩| ≤ r, |⟨w, e⟩| ≤ r}, a closed (so measurable) set. As in step 5, ι^{-1}(K_r) = {v : |v₀| ≤ r, |v₁| ≤ r} (because |v|² ≤ 2r² ≤ 8 ≤ 9), which corresponds to the box [−r, r]² = Icc (fun _ => −r) (fun _ => r) of volume ofReal(2r)·ofReal(2r) = ofReal(4r²) (Real.volume_Icc_pi). Hence ν₀(K_r) = ofReal(4r²). ∎
proof_key_steps: (a, e) is an orthonormal basis of Q, so ι(v) = v₀a + v₁e is an isometry of EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin 2) onto Q with ⟨ι v, a⟩ = v₀, ⟨ι v, e⟩ = v₁.
For measurable S, ν₀(S) = μHE[2](ι(ι^{-1}S)) = vol₂(ι^{-1}S) (isometry invariance; μHE[2] = volume in dimension 2).
For compact K, ι^{-1}K is bounded, so ν₀(K) < ∞.
For 0 ≤ r ≤ 2 the ball constraint is redundant on Q (2r² ≤ 8 < 9), so the preimages are the boxes (−r, r)² and [−r, r]², of volume 4r².

subproblems.title: Portmanteau bounds for the rescaled measures λ_j^{-2}(η_j)_#μ
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ, μ and ν measures on ℝ^P that are finite on compact sets, a ∈ ℝ^P and λ_j > 0 (j ∈ ℕ); put η_j := dilation a λ_j. Assume that λ_j^{-2}∫ g(η_j(x)) dμ(x) → ∫ g dν for every continuous compactly supported g : ℝ^P → ℝ. Then limsup_j ofReal(λ_j^{-2})·μ(η_j^{-1}(K)) ≤ ν(K) for every compact K, and ν(U) ≤ liminf_j ofReal(λ_j^{-2})·μ(η_j^{-1}(U)) for every open U.
subproblems.lean_statement: ∀ (P : ℕ) (μ ν : Measure (Euclid P)) (a : Euclid P) (lams : ℕ → ℝ), IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts μ → IsFiniteMeasureOnCompacts ν → (∀ j, 0 < lams j) → (∀ g : Euclid P → ℝ, Continuous g → HasCompactSupport g → Tendsto (fun j => (lams j)⁻¹ ^ 2 * ∫ x, g (dilation a (lams j) x) ∂μ) atTop (𝓝 (∫ x, g x ∂ν))) → (∀ K : Set (Euclid P), IsCompact K → limsup (fun j => ENNReal.ofReal ((lams j)⁻¹ ^ 2) * μ (dilation a (lams j) ⁻¹' K)) atTop ≤ ν K) ∧ ∀ U : Set (Euclid P), IsOpen U → ν U ≤ liminf (fun j => ENNReal.ofReal ((lams j)⁻¹ ^ 2) * μ (dilation a (lams j) ⁻¹' U)) atTop
subproblems.natural_proof:
1. (η_j is a homeomorphism.) η_j(y) = −(λ_j^{-1}•a) + λ_j^{-1}•y is the linear homeomorphism y ↦ λ_j^{-1}y (λ_j ≠ 0) followed by a translation (Homeomorph.smulOfNeZero composed with Homeomorph.addLeft), so η_j is a homeomorphism of ℝ^P. Hence η_j is continuous, measurable and proper: η_j^{-1}(K) is compact for every compact K.
2. (Rescaled push-forwards.) Let c_j := ofReal(λ_j^{-2}) and ν_j := (η_j)_#(c_j·μ) (Measure.map). For measurable S, ν_j(S) = c_j·μ(η_j^{-1}(S)) (Measure.map_apply, η_j measurable).
3. (Local finiteness.) For compact K (closed, hence measurable), ν_j(K) = c_j·μ(η_j^{-1}(K)) < ∞, because c_j < ∞, η_j^{-1}(K) is compact (step 1) and μ is finite on compact sets.
4. (Integrals.) Let g be continuous with compact support. subproblems.title: The boxes Z(s, s') have mass asymptotic to 4m s'²

For s' ∈ ℝ let Z(s, s') := {x : ⟨x, a⟩ > 0, ||x| − 1| < s', |arctan(⟨x, e⟩/⟨x, a⟩)| < s', |x − πx| < s|x|}. Assume (L) μ(Z(s, s') ∖ B_{3s'}(a)) = 0 for every 0 < s' ≤ s, and (V) for every sequence λ_j > 0 with λ_j → 0 there is a strictly increasing φ such that λ_{φ(j)}^{-2}∫ g(dilation a λ_{φ(j)} x) dμ(x) → m∫_Q g dH² for every continuous compactly supported g : ℝ^P → ℝ. 1. (Reduction.) By the sibling subseq_criterion (Submission.idtp_cse_bml_tendsto_nhdsGT_of_subseq) with f := H and L := 4m, it suffices to show: for every sequence λ_j > 0 with λ_j → 0 there is a strictly increasing φ with H(λ_{φ(j)}) → 4m.
2. Fix such (λ_j). Take φ from (V) and put t_j := λ_{φ(j)}; then t_j > 0 and t_j → 0 (φ strictly increasing, so φ(j) → ∞).
3. (The limit measure.) By the sibling square_measure, H²⌞Q is finite on compact sets; hence so is ν (ν(K) = m·(H²⌞Q)(K) < ∞). For measurable S, ν(S) = m·(H²⌞Q)(S) (Measure.smul_apply). subproblems.natural_proof:
1. For v : Fin 2 → ℝ^P put f(v) := ⟨a, v 0⟩⟨e, v 1⟩ − ⟨a, v 1⟩⟨e, v 0⟩.
2. (Multilinear.) Fix i ∈ Fin 2 = {0, 1} and the other entry. Each of the two products in f contains exactly one factor depending on v i, namely ⟨a, v i⟩ or ⟨e, v i⟩, which is linear in v i (linearity of the inner product in its second argument). Hence replacing v i by x + y (resp. c•x) turns f into the sum of the two values (resp. c times the value); this is checked by the two cases i = 0, i = 1 and ring normalization.
3. (Alternating.) If v i = v j with i ≠ j, then {i, j} = {0, 1}, so v 0 = v 1 =: u and f(v) = ⟨a, u⟩⟨e, u⟩ − ⟨a, u⟩⟨e, u⟩ = 0. So f is an alternating map ℝ^P [⋀^Fin 2]→ₗ[ℝ] ℝ.
4. (Bound.) By the triangle inequality and Cauchy–Schwarz, |f(v)| ≤ |⟨a, v 0⟩||⟨e, v 1⟩| + |⟨a, v 1⟩||⟨e, v 0⟩| ≤ 2|a||e|·|v 0||v 1| = (2|a||e|)·∏_i |v i|.
5. Hence β := AlternatingMap.mkContinuous f (2|a||e|) (step 4) is a continuous alternating map, i.e. β ∈ Covector(ℝ^P, 2), and β(v) = f(v) for all v (coe_mkContinuous), which is the required formula. ∎

f vanishes when v₀ = v₁, so f is an alternating map.
|f(v)| ≤ 2|a||e||v₀||v₁|, so AlternatingMap.mkContinuous yields β ∈ Covector(ℝ^P, 2) agreeing with f.

subproblems.title: Pointwise tilt bound 1 − G ≤ 2(1 − |ξ(β)|) under radial tangency
subproblems.statement: Let P ∈ ℕ and R = (M, θ, ξ) an IMRep of dimension 2 in ℝ^P (U = univ), μ := R.measure, T_x := approxTangentPlane 2 M x with orthogonal projection p_{T_x}. Let Q be a linear subspace with dim Q = 2 and orthogonal projection π, a, e ∈ Q with |a| = |e| = 1 and ⟨a, e⟩ = 0, and β ∈ Covector(ℝ^P, 2) with β(v) = ⟨a, v₀⟩⟨e, v₁⟩ − ⟨a, v₁⟩⟨e, v₀⟩ for all v : Fin 2 → ℝ^P. Assume p_{T_x}x = x for μ-a.e. x. Put Ax := ⟨x, a⟩e − ⟨x, e⟩a and G(x) := |p_{T_x}(Ax)|²/|πx|². Then (i) G(x) ≤ 1 for every x with ⟨x, a⟩ > 0; (ii) for μ-a.e. x: |ξ(x)(β)| ≤ 1, and if ⟨x, a⟩ > 0 then 1 − 2(1 − |ξ(x)(β)|) ≤ G(x).

subproblems.natural_proof:
Notation: d(x) := ξ(x)(β) = R.orient x β.
1. (Basis of Q.) a and e are orthonormal, hence linearly independent; span{a, e} ⊆ Q has dimension 2 = dim Q, so span{a, e} = Q and (a, e) is an orthonormal basis of Q. Hence πx = ⟨x, a⟩a + ⟨x, e⟩e and |πx|² = ⟨x, a⟩² + ⟨x, e⟩² for all x.
2. |Ax|² = ⟨x, a⟩²|e|² − 2⟨x, a⟩⟨x, e⟩⟨a, e⟩ + ⟨x, e⟩²|a|² = ⟨x, a⟩² + ⟨x, e⟩² = |πx|².
3. (Claim (i).) Let ⟨x, a⟩ > 0. Then |πx|² ≥ ⟨x, a⟩² > 0. An orthogonal projection does not increase norms (also when T_x = ⊥, where p_{T_x} = 0), so |p_{T_x}(Ax)|² ≤ |Ax|² = |πx|², i.e. G(x) ≤ 1.
4. (A full-measure set.) μ = (H²⌞M).withDensity θ, so μ ≪ H²⌞M (withDensity_absolutelyContinuous; also the first conjunct of the accepted Submission.cbr_imRep_measure_basic). The field R.orients holds for H²⌞M-a.e. x, hence for μ-a.e. x; the hypothesis gives p_{T_x}x = x for μ-a.e. x. Fix x at which both hold: there is Q' with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt 2 M x Q' and IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(x)) Q', and p_{T_x}x = x. It suffices to prove the two assertions of (ii) at such x.
5. (T_x = Q'.) Since ∃ Q', HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt 2 M x Q', by definition approxTangentPlane 2 M x is a chosen Q'' with HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt 2 M x Q''; by uniqueness of approximate tangent spaces (Poincare.SimonGMT.Chapter03.HasApproximateTangentSpaceAt.unique, Simon Ch. 3 Remark 1.5(1)), Q'' = Q'. So T_x = Q'.
6. (Orientation.) IsUnitOrientationOf (ξ(x)) T_x gives τ : Fin 2 → ℝ^P orthonormal with span{τ₀, τ₁} = T_x and a sign σ ∈ {1, −1} with ξ(x)(α) = σ·α(τ) for all covectors α. Put a_i := ⟨a, τ_i⟩, e_i := ⟨e, τ_i⟩ and D := a₀e₁ − a₁e₀. By the hypothesis on β, d(x) = σ·β(τ) = σD, so |d(x)| = |D| and d(x)² = D².
7. (|d| ≤ 1.) Lagrange's identity: (a₀² + a₁²)(e₀² + e₁²) − D² = (a₀e₀ + a₁e₁)² ≥ 0. By Bessel's inequality for the orthonormal family τ, a₀² + a₁² ≤ |a|² = 1 and e₀² + e₁² ≤ |e|² = 1. Hence D² ≤ 1, i.e. |d(x)| ≤ 1.
8. (Coordinates in T_x.) τ is an orthonormal basis of T_x, so p_{T_x}v = ⟨v, τ₀⟩τ₀ + ⟨v, τ₁⟩τ₁ and |p_{T_x}v|² = ⟨v, τ₀⟩² + ⟨v, τ₁⟩² for all v. Since p_{T_x}x = x, with x_i := ⟨x, τ_i⟩ we have x = x₀τ₀ + x₁τ₁, |x|² = x₀² + x₁², ⟨x, a⟩ = x₀a₀ + x₁a₁ and ⟨x, e⟩ = x₀e₀ + x₁e₁.
9. (Computation.) ⟨Ax, τ₀⟩ = ⟨x, a⟩e₀ − ⟨x, e⟩a₀ = (x₀a₀ + x₁a₁)e₀ − (x₀e₀ + x₁e₁)a₀ = x₁(a₁e₀ − a₀e₁) = −x₁D, and ⟨Ax, τ₁⟩ = (x₀a₀ + x₁a₁)e₁ − (x₀e₀ + x₁e₁)a₁ = x₀(a₀e₁ − a₁e₀) = x₀D. Hence |p_{T_x}(Ax)|² = D²(x₀² + x₁²) = D²|x|².
10. (Second part of (ii).) Let moreover ⟨x, a⟩ > 0. Then 0 < |πx| (step 3) and |πx| ≤ |x| (projection), so G(x) = D²|x|²/|πx|² ≥ D² = d(x)². Finally 1 − 2(1 − |d(x)|) = 2|d(x)| − 1 ≤ d(x)², because d(x)² − 2|d(x)| + 1 = (|d(x)| − 1)² ≥ 0. Therefore 1 − 2(1 − |d(x)|) ≤ G(x). ∎
proof_key_steps: (a, e) is an orthonormal basis of Q, so |πx|² = ⟨x, a⟩² + ⟨x, e⟩² = |Ax|²; projections are 1-Lipschitz, so G ≤ 1 where ⟨x, a⟩ > 0.
μ ≪ H²⌞M transfers R.orients; with radial tangency and uniqueness of approximate tangent planes, a.e. T_x has an orthonormal basis τ with ξ(x)(β) = ±D, D = ⟨a, τ₀⟩⟨e, τ₁⟩ − ⟨a, τ₁⟩⟨e, τ₀⟩.
